questions.q: What is this course's throughline, across all 30 lessons?
options: Taking the real-time ingestion idea Fabric's Eventstreams already introduced and teaching Kafka's own architecture as the vendor-neutral version of that same idea
Re-teaching windowing, watermarks, and streaming concepts entirely from scratch
Replacing the need to ever use Microsoft Fabric
Teaching a brand-new streaming concept unrelated to anything covered in the Azure/Fabric Data Engineer path
questions.explain: This course explicitly assumed the streaming concepts Fabric & Real-Time Analytics already taught, and built Kafka's own vocabulary and architecture on top of that foundation.

questions.q: What did the capstone project (Lesson 29) actually prove, according to this lesson?
options: That this course's own decisions — producer configuration, topic sizing, error handling — actually compose into one real, working pipeline
That dead-letter topics are unnecessary in a real pipeline
That consumer groups should never be used together with idempotent producers
That this course's ideas only apply to clickstream data and nowhere else
questions.explain: The capstone is proof the earlier 28 lessons' techniques work together — and that the same shape generalizes to a real system like Career & Capstone's fraud detector.

questions.q: Does finishing this course complete the entire Azure/Fabric Data Engineer career path, according to this lesson's verification?
options: Yes — Git/GitHub/CI-CD, Terraform & Bicep, and Airflow were already built, so finishing Kafka completes both the Job Ready and Advanced stages, all 10 courses
No — Terraform & Bicep still needs to be built after this course
No — this course has no relationship to the Azure/Fabric Data Engineer path at all
Yes, but only the Job Ready stage — the Advanced stage still has courses remaining
questions.explain: All three of the other Advanced-stage courses were already complete before this course started, and the Job Ready stage was already complete as well — Kafka was the last piece.

questions.q: What structure does this lesson suggest for presenting the capstone in an interview?
options: The same project-story structure from Career & Capstone Lesson 80 — situation, design decisions, trade-offs, what you'd change — applied to Kafka-specific decisions
Reciting the entire producer and consumer code line by line with no explanation
Only mentioning that the project used Kafka, without any other detail
There is no recommended structure — improvise entirely
questions.explain: Kafka-specific decisions worth naming out loud include partition counts, the producer's delivery guarantees, and why a dead-letter topic was used instead of infinite retries.

questions.q: Why does this lesson have no "Check yourself" question, unlike every other lesson in the course?
options: There's no next lesson in this course or next course in the path's core sequence — readiness is instead being able to explain the capstone's own code to someone else
This lesson was left unfinished on purpose
Check-yourself questions are only used in Chapter 1
The quiz below replaces the need for any written guide content
questions.explain: Every other lesson's 'Check yourself' question checks readiness for what comes next — the finale has no next lesson or course to prepare for.
